agenda.item: Opening prayer and wins of the month
Hot seat: Jake's food truck permit plan
Book discussion: The E-Myth Revisited, ch. 1-4

hotSeatPrep.problem: Should I lease a used truck now or run a pop-up tent at the farmers market for a season first?
hotSeatPrep.context: I've saved $14k. A used truck lease is $1,900/month plus a $6k build-out. The farmers market spot is $85 a Saturday.
hotSeatPrep.whatTried: Priced three trucks, talked to two owners at the county fair, wrote a rough menu of six items.
hotSeatPrep.winLooksLike: A clear yes or no on the truck, and a test I can run before Thanksgiving.

agenda.item: Opening prayer and wins of the month
Hot seat: Sarah's bookkeeping side business pricing

hotSeatPrep.problem: I have 6 clients at $150/month. Do I raise prices for new clients only, or for everyone in January?
hotSeatPrep.context: Every client takes 5-7 hours a month. Local bookkeepers charge $250-400. I'm scared of losing the two church clients.
hotSeatPrep.whatTried: Looked up three competitors and tracked my hours for August.
hotSeatPrep.winLooksLike: A price I can say out loud without flinching, and a script for telling current clients.

adviceTaken: Raise new clients to $250 starting now
Give current clients 60 days notice for January
Offer the church clients a nonprofit rate
actionPlan.nextStep: Email all current clients the new January pricing.

agenda.item: Opening prayer and wins of the month
Hot seat: Daniel's rental property decision

hotSeatPrep.problem: The duplex on Maple needs $18k in repairs. Do we fix and rent it, or sell as-is and put the money into the second lot?
hotSeatPrep.context: Bought it in 2019 for $142k. Comparable rentals get $1,150 per side. Roof and one furnace are the big items.
hotSeatPrep.whatTried: Got one rough quote and asked a realtor for an as-is number ($205k).
hotSeatPrep.winLooksLike: A decision we both feel good about and a deadline to make it by.

adviceTaken: Get a second contractor bid before deciding
Run the numbers at 8% vacancy, not zero
Ask the realtor what a fixed-up unit would sell for
actionPlan.nextStep: Get two contractor bids on the Maple duplex repairs.

asks.title: Anyone know a commercial kitchen I can rent by the hour?
asks.detail: The pop-ups are outgrowing Mom's kitchen. Looking for something near Elm Grove under $25/hour.

replies.text: The church kitchen sits empty on weekdays. I'll ask Pastor Dave.
Try the culinary school on 4th. They rented to a caterer we know.

asks.title: Mock interview for a product manager role
asks.detail: I have a first-round interview on Nov 12. Would love 30 minutes with someone who's hired people before.

asks.title: Need a second van for Nov 21
asks.detail: We have 14 people going to the food bank and room for 8.

replies.text: Our minivan seats 7. It's yours that day.

asks.title: Which Roth IRA provider should I use?
asks.detail: Fidelity, Vanguard or Schwab? I want low fees and an app that's easy.

replies.text: Any of the three is fine. Fidelity has no minimum and a good app.
Pick a target-date fund and leave it alone.

announcements.title: November meeting moves to the Whitakers'
announcements.body: Our kitchen is getting new floors that week, so Hannah and Tom are hosting Nov 8. Same time, 3:00. Bring a chair if you have a folding one. Linda is doing chili, so sides and desserts are welcome.

comments.text: We're excited. Park on the street, the driveway will be full of the van.
I'll bring cornbread from the pop-up batch.
I can come straight from the clinic, might be 15 min late.

announcements.title: Food bank shift is confirmed for Nov 21
announcements.body: We have the 9:00 to 12:00 shift at Northside Food Bank for all of us. Closed-toe shoes, no jewelry. Kids 10 and up can work the sorting line. Lunch at Mom and Dad's after.

comments.text: Thank you for setting this up. This is my favorite day of the year.
Can I bring my friend Marcus? He needs service hours.
Yes! Just send me his full name for the sign-in list.

announcements.title: Q3 family fund summary is ready
announcements.body: The fund finished the quarter up 4.1%. I wrote a one-page summary with a plain-English note on why the bond fund dipped. Paper copies at the meeting, or ask me for the PDF.

comments.text: Clear and short. This is exactly what we needed.

announcements.title: Welcome to the app
announcements.body: This is where we'll keep the agenda, our commitments and the hot seat schedule from now on. Check in before each meeting and keep your commitment status current. Questions go to me or Emily.

comments.text: Happy to help anyone get it on their phone.

ideas.title: Wave for simple invoicing
ideas.note: Free invoicing that a lot of my small clients use. Good for Jake once the truck takes catering orders.

ideas.title: How I Built This: the Chobani episode
ideas.note: A small-town factory bought with an SBA loan. Made me think of Daniel's lot.

ideas.title: Write our family mission in one sentence
ideas.note: Before we set 2027 goals, agree on one sentence about why this group exists. Then each goal should point at it.

comments.text: Let's put it on the November agenda.
I'll bring a few examples from other families.

ideas.title: Roth IRA for students: the 5-minute version
ideas.note: Grace asked about this. Short, no sales pitch.

ideas.title: Pre-orders by text for Saturday pop-ups
ideas.note: I keep running out by 1pm. Taking pre-orders on Friday night would tell me how much to cook.

ideas.title: County permit lookup
ideas.note: You can see every permit pulled on a property. Useful before buying anything older.

ideas.title: Lawn care price sheet from Tyler's dad
ideas.note: He charges $45 a cut for a quarter acre and $120 for leaf cleanup. I'm going to start lower.

comments.text: Don't start too low. It's hard to raise later.

books.title: The Psychology of Money
books.author: Morgan Housel
books.why: Short chapters, no math. Best book I know for getting the whole family on the same page about money.

comments.text: Read it twice. Let's discuss chapter 6 in November.

books.title: The E-Myth Revisited
books.author: Michael E. Gerber
books.why: Every small business owner I work with should read it before they hire anyone.

comments.text: The part about working on vs in your business is my commitment this month.

books.title: Atomic Habits
books.author: James Clear
books.why: Small habits are how we keep commitments between meetings.

books.title: Die With Zero
books.author: Bill Perkins
books.why: Challenges how Linda and I think about giving while we're alive. I'd like the kids' take.

books.title: Inspired
books.author: Marty Cagan
books.why: The book every product manager interview seems to assume you've read.

books.title: Kitchen Confidential
books.author: Anthony Bourdain
books.why: What working a line is really like. Fun read even if you never cook.

books.title: The Richest Man in Babylon
books.author: George S. Clason
books.why: Grandpa gave me this at 18. Old, short and still right.

comments.text: Finished it on the bus. Pay yourself first.
